question: What is the primary function of diagnostic devices in clinical practice?

options.A: To provide objective physiological data for health evaluation
options.B: To replace the need for physical nursing assessments
options.D: To permanently store patient financial records

explanation: Diagnostic devices generate measurable and quantifiable data that complement physical examinations and support clinical decision-making. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T1#GNS113_U4_T1_h1)

question: Which item is classified as a physiological monitoring device?
explanation: Electrocardiogram machines continuously track and record the electrical activity of the heart, placing them in the physiological monitor category. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T1#GNS113_U4_T1_h1)

question: What is the primary advantage of point-of-care testing at the bedside?

options.A: Lower cost of manufacturing compared to large laboratory machines
options.B: Rapid availability of diagnostic results for immediate care
options.C: Complete removal of human error in result interpretation
options.D: Elimination of the need for infection control protocols

explanation: Performing diagnostics at the bedside bypasses transport and processing delays, allowing clinicians to act on results almost instantly. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T1#GNS113_U4_T1_h2)

question: A nurse needs to assess a patient's non-invasive arterial oxygen saturation. Which device is selected?
explanation: A pulse oximeter uses light wavelengths to calculate hemoglobin oxygen saturation through the skin without drawing blood. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T1#GNS113_U4_T1_h2)

question: What type of energy does an ultrasound device use to create internal body images?
explanation: Ultrasound equipment transmits acoustic waves into tissue and measures the returning echoes to form a visual display. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T1#GNS113_U4_T1_h3)

question: Why is ultrasound frequently preferred over standard X-rays for monitoring pregnant women?

options.A: It provides a permanent chemical analysis of amniotic fluid
options.B: It produces three-dimensional color images automatically
options.C: It does not expose the fetus to ionizing radiation
options.D: It is completely painless and requires no gel application

explanation: Ultrasound operates purely on sound waves, avoiding the cellular risks associated with ionizing radiation during pregnancy. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T1#GNS113_U4_T1_h3)

question: Which imaging modality utilizes powerful magnetic fields and radiofrequency waves?
explanation: MRIs align hydrogen protons in the body using a strong magnetic field and manipulate them with radiofrequency energy to form images. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T1#GNS113_U4_T1_h4)

question: A patient scheduled for an upcoming magnetic resonance imaging scan must be screened primarily for which hazard?

options.A: Exposure to natural sunlight within the last week
options.C: Recent consumption of high-fat dairy products
options.D: Embedded metallic medical devices or foreign objects

explanation: The powerful magnetic force of an MRI machine can dislodge metal implants or heat up conductive objects, posing severe safety risks. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T1#GNS113_U4_T1_h4)

question: What is the primary purpose of a Picture Archiving and Communication System (PACS) in a hospital?

options.A: To monitor patient vital signs in real-time intensive care
options.B: To store, retrieve, and distribute digital medical images
options.C: To automatically order laboratory blood tests for patients
options.D: To calculate daily nursing staff shift rosters and hours

explanation: PACS functions as a specialized digital repository designed specifically to manage and share diagnostic imaging files across networks. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T1#GNS113_U4_T1_h5)

question: How does the integration of diagnostic devices with electronic health records improve patient safety?

options.A: It removes all requirements for manual patient identification checks
options.B: It completely prevents any equipment calibration errors by staff
options.C: It ensures instant access to verified test results at the point of care
options.D: It automates the physical administration of intravenous drugs

explanation: Seamless digital integration reduces transcription delays and ensures clinical teams review accurate, up-to-date diagnostic data. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T1#GNS113_U4_T1_h5)

question: Why is routine calibration of diagnostic devices strictly necessary?

options.A: To increase the market financial value of the machine
options.B: To extend the physical lifespan of plastic outer casings
options.C: To eliminate the need for routine equipment cleaning
options.D: To ensure the accuracy and reliability of clinical readings

explanation: Calibration checks sensor and hardware performance against established standards to prevent erroneous diagnostic data. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T1#GNS113_U4_T1_h6)

question: Which of the following is NOT an appropriate nursing action regarding diagnostic device safety?

options.A: Checking for valid calibration tags before operating complex monitors
options.B: Reporting malfunctioning hardware to biomedical engineering promptly
options.C: Ensuring patient privacy when displaying digital imaging results
options.D: Using equipment with frayed electrical cords if it still turns on

explanation: Damaged electrical cords present severe shock and fire hazards and must never be used on patients, regardless of whether the device powers on. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T1#GNS113_U4_T1_h6)
